newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle close higher.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle close higher.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures closed higher as expectations of a firmer undertone to fed cattle supported the markets, traders said.
Live cattle closed 0.375 to 0.050 cent per lb higher with June up most at 65.825 cents. Feeder cattle posted gains of 0.125 to 0.675 with August up 0.650 at 77.475 cents.

Reports that packers raised their bids up to $67 per cwt early and continued expectations by some traders that $68 will be paid for cattle this week supported live cattle futures. Mostly higher boxed beef values to start the week also lent some support, they said.

Cargill Investor Services and Refco bought June late while R.J. O'Brien was on both sides of the market and RBH sold. Rosenthal Collins and ADM Investor Services bought August and Prudential Securities sold while buying December on a spread. Refco also spread long December/short August and other spreaders bought August and sold June, pit sources said.

In live cattle options, commercials were doing the October risk reversal, buying 68 puts and selling 72 calls. Commission houses sold June 66 calls with volatility in June down one percent to nine percent, considered historically low for the time period before expiration, pit sources added.

Feeder cattle futures rose on lack of sell interest and spillover support from higher live cattle futures and lower corn futures early. Strength in feeders came despite expectations the next CME feeder cattle index would show a large decline, traders said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.27 to $77.64 per cwt, its highest level since August 23, 1994. Expectations are for the index to fall about $1.50 in the next quote.
Refco bought August early with Cargill spreading, buying August and selling May. Prudential also did the spread later. Rosenthal bought August at the close, pit sources said.
